title: What's cooking 🍳
intro: The automations I'm building to take the grunt work out of measurement, from the first tracking plan to the last health check. Tap any one to see what it does and why it helps.

groups.heading: The measurement pipeline
groups.blurb: Eleven pieces that take a client from brief to trustworthy data, in the order they run.

projects.name: Measurement plan, event spec and data dictionary
projects.next: Refining it, and customising it to each client's needs.
projects.summary: Turns a client brief and a site audit into a measurement plan, an event spec and a data dictionary.
does: Reads the client brief and the site audit
Maps business goals to KPIs, then to the events and parameters that measure them
Writes the event spec and a data dictionary with consistent naming
Becomes the single source of truth that every later step builds from
benefits: Days of planning becomes hours
The same naming rules across every client
Everything downstream (GTM, dev briefs, tests) traces back to one approved plan

projects.name: GTM container builder
projects.summary: Builds the Tag Manager container (tags, triggers and variables) straight from the approved tracking plan.
does: Reads the approved tracking plan
Creates the tags, triggers and variables to match it exactly
Sets consent requirements on every tag
Outputs a container that imports in one step
benefits: No more hand-building tags one by one
The container always matches the spec
Easy to rebuild when the plan changes

projects.name: GA4 + GTM audit
projects.summary: Checks existing Tag Manager containers and GA4 set-up, built in Apps Script and in use today.
does: Reviews GTM containers: tags, triggers, variables, naming, duplicates, unused items and consent settings
Reviews the GA4 property: data streams, events, key events, custom definitions, retention and product links
Checks everything against a fixed rule set, so the result is deterministic
Looks at configuration only, never personal data
benefits: Hours of clicking through admin screens becomes minutes
Re-run it after changes and compare like with like
Catches gaps before they quietly cost months of data

projects.name: Developer briefs and ticketing
projects.next: Waiting on build time. Next up: generating the briefs, then exploring Jira and Confluence.
projects.summary: Turns an approved tracking plan into a ready-to-brief spec for developers.
does: Writes a developer brief per event: the dataLayer code to add, where it fires and what each value should be
Adds acceptance criteria and test steps so 'done' is clear
Exploring: creating Jira tickets and Confluence pages automatically, linked back to the plan
benefits: Developers get exactly what they need, first time
Every ticket traces back to an approved line in the plan
Far less back-and-forth between analysts and developers

projects.name: Automated website overview, audit and testing
projects.summary: A robot browser that runs through a site to check the dataLayer and tracking fire correctly. It also works as a standalone audit tool.
does: Opens pages and runs key journeys (page views, clicks, forms, checkout) like a real visitor
Watches network requests to see which tags fired and what they sent
Checks the dataLayer at each step against the spec
Reads the site's Content Security Policy and flags any vendor it would block
Works in Tag Manager preview before release, and on the live site to diagnose problems
benefits: Tests changes before they go live
Diagnoses production issues in minutes
Catches silent breakages, like a release that kills a conversion tag

projects.name: Conversational analytics: event health
projects.summary: Ask plain-English questions about event health and get validated answers back. Done and in use.
does: Runs on Google's Conversational Analytics API over BigQuery, with no Looker licence needed
Answers questions like 'which events dropped this week?' or 'is purchase missing currency?'
Validates its answers before showing them
benefits: Event health without writing SQL
Answers you can trust, because they're checked
Much cheaper than an enterprise BI licence

projects.name: Event-health monitoring and alerts
projects.summary: Checks event health on demand and flags issues. Built on Gemini.
does: Runs health checks across key events when prompted
Flags drops, spikes, missing parameters and broken values
Runs on request rather than always-on, to keep costs under control
benefits: Problems surface before a report goes out wrong
Cost stays predictable
Pairs with the conversational analytics agent for follow-up questions

projects.name: Agent evaluation + Cloud Run AI harness
projects.summary: Runs the agents at scale in the cloud instead of on a laptop, and scores how well they answer.
does: Runs batches of test questions against an agent on Cloud Run
Scores the answers and flags made-up ones
Tracks the Google Cloud cost of each agent and each run
benefits: Find weak spots before people rely on an agent
Scale testing without tying up anyone's machine
Costs are visible, not a surprise on the bill

projects.name: GA4 config updates on approval
projects.summary: Pushes approved GA4 configuration changes live in a property automatically.
does: Takes a set of approved changes (events, key events, custom definitions, settings)
Applies them to the GA4 property only after sign-off
Keeps a record of what changed and when
benefits: No manual clicking through GA4 admin
Changes match exactly what was approved
A clear audit trail of every change

projects.name: Enterprise BigQuery set-up + knowledge graph
projects.next: Client-requested. Researching what can be automated.
projects.summary: Stands up the BigQuery structure and a knowledge graph in Google Cloud directly from a client's tracking definitions.
does: Reads the tracking definitions from the data dictionary
Creates the BigQuery datasets, tables and data-engineering fields to match
Builds a knowledge graph so business terms, events and tables are linked
benefits: Warehouse and tracking stay in sync by design
Agents and analysts share the same definitions
Weeks of set-up shrinks once it's automated

projects.name: Client-specific GA4 / GMP / GCP news summary
projects.summary: Pulls the latest GA4, Google Marketing Platform and Google Cloud news into a client-ready summary.
does: Searches a fixed window across Google release notes, practitioners and trusted publications
Keeps only what changed, with every item dated and sourced
Explains what it means for that client and what to do about it
benefits: Clients hear about changes from you first
Staying current takes a read, not a day of searching
The same engine behind On the Pulse

groups.heading: Side experiments
groups.blurb: Things I'm trying on my own time.

projects.name: BigQuery agents with a custom front end
projects.summary: Turning the conversational analytics agents into a proper product, not just a chat window.
does: A custom interface with filters, and an intent agent that works out what you're really asking
A semantic layer so business terms mean one thing
Purpose-built agents, like segmentation, health checks and explaining BigQuery billing spikes
benefits: Self-serve answers for people who don't write SQL
The same patterns I teach in my BigQuery agents workshops

projects.name: UTM naming checker
projects.summary: Catches messy campaign tags before they split reporting into a hundred versions of 'Facebook'.
does: Reads naming rules from a Google Sheet marketers can update
Checks every UTM combination in the GA4 BigQuery export with SQL
Flags typos, wrong case and unknown values, with the traffic each affects
Answers follow-up questions through BigQuery's built-in Gemini agent
benefits: Clean channel reporting without monthly clean-up
Marketers own the rules; no code edits
Shows the cost of bad tagging, so fixes get prioritised

projects.name: Data Agent Kit experiments
projects.summary: Testing Google's new Data Agent Kit, which lets coding agents query, build pipelines and do data science on BigQuery.
does: Connects a coding agent to BigQuery with Google's own skills and tools
Puts guardrails in first: an IAM policy blocking write actions
benefits: Finds out what's useful versus demo-only
Compares Google with Snowflake, Databricks and Microsoft

projects.name: Personal dashboard + automated data warehouse
projects.summary: My own data flowing into BigQuery on a schedule, with a dashboard that's always up to date.
does: Pulls data into BigQuery automatically
Models it with version-controlled SQL
Feeds a dashboard that refreshes itself
benefits: No copy-paste reporting
A sandbox for testing new tools on real data

outro: Got a tool you'd like to see here, or want to compare notes? Leave a comment on the latest edition.
